votes.evidence:
It is true that the task does not re-check the toggle. `process_inbox_pr_review` (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1110-1200) never reads the toggle again. It trusts the check that review_hog's receiver ran on the save path (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:126, which calls `_start_stamphog_review` via on_commit, then `queue_inbox_pr_review`). The docstring at tasks.py:1115-1117 says so.

The claim that this differs from the webhook path does not hold:
- The webhook carve-out also checks the toggle only once, when the delivery is processed (`_inbox_rereview_carve_out`, tasks.py:201-204, through `resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer` at receivers.py:147-160).
- After that check, both paths do the same thing. They create a ReviewRun with `output["inbox_review"]` provenance and start the Temporal workflow on commit.
- The workflow and its activities never re-check the toggle. They only read `inbox_review` provenance (products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:175, 237, 451).
- On both paths, the gap between the toggle check and the posted approval is mostly the sandbox review itself, which takes minutes. On the inbox path the Celery queue delay adds only a little.

So both paths answer the gate question once, before the long step. Neither re-checks before posting, and the gap the finding points at is small next to that shared one.

AGENTS.md (products/stamphog/AGENTS.md ~100-110) only promises that switching the toggle off "stops new runs". A run that was already dispatched is effectively in flight on either path, and the dismissal rules still apply. Posting an approval only needs a toggle flipped in a seconds-wide window after a TaskRun save, which is an unlikely race.
votes.refutation:
This is not a real gap between the two paths. The webhook carve-out (tasks.py:201-204) also checks the toggle once, before it creates the run. From there both paths go through the same Temporal workflow, and that workflow never re-checks the toggle before posting the approval (activities.py:175/237/451 only read the `inbox_review` provenance).

The inbox path's extra window is only the Celery queue delay, and each path already has the longer sandbox run between check and approval. Neither path re-checks there, so this does not break the documented "stops new runs" rule.

Adding a re-check at the start of the task would not close the larger gap. Triggering the issue needs someone to flip the toggle within a few seconds of the dispatch, which is too unlikely to count as a defect.

votes.evidence: The receiver leg does check the toggle once, when the TaskRun output is saved (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:126). It then queues `process_inbox_pr_review` on commit (receivers.py:131-139), and that task never checks the toggle again (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1109-1200). The webhook leg's check has the same shape. `_resolve_inbox_carve_out` calls the resolver once per delivery (tasks.py:201-205), stamps provenance, and creates the run with `transaction.on_commit(_start_review_workflow)` (tasks.py:1064-1073). Neither leg checks the toggle again during the Temporal review workflow. That workflow runs a sandbox and an LLM, so it takes minutes, and the GitHub review is posted at its end. A toggle switched off in that window still gets an approval posted on either leg.
votes.refutation: The claim that the two legs answer the gate question "at different times" does not hold up in any way that matters. Both legs check once and then act later without checking again. The receiver leg adds only the Celery broker delay (normally seconds). That is small next to the multi-minute review workflow that follows on both legs, and the proposed fix would not cover that workflow. The trigger needs the acting reviewer to switch the toggle off in the seconds between the implementation run saving its PR URL and the Celery task being picked up. That is a speculative race with no realistic trigger. The approval is the Stamphog App's review, which the reviewer opted into, not a credential the user owns. Existing safety still applies: on later head changes, a toggle that is off routes to the skip path, and that path dismisses the stale approval (tasks.py:161-165 docstring). The finding's own entry already carries is_valid=false.

votes.evidence: The code does what the finding says. `process_inbox_pr_review` (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1110-1240) never re-checks `stamphog_review_inbox_prs`. The only check happens at dispatch, in review_hog/backend/receivers.py:126, inside a `transaction.on_commit` enqueue. The webhook path re-checks through the resolver inside the Celery task (tasks.py:201-204).
votes.refutation: The window the finding describes is not a real gap in production. (1) The trigger needs the acting reviewer to turn the toggle off in the gap between the TaskRun output save and the Celery worker picking up the task. With a healthy broker that is seconds, and the PR in question was opened moments earlier under their opt-in. (2) The webhook path has the same kind of gap, only longer. It checks the toggle once in the Celery task (tasks.py:201-204), then creates the ReviewRun and starts a Temporal workflow (tasks.py:1073). The sandbox and LLM review runs for minutes after that and never re-checks before posting the approval. So a recheck at the start of `process_inbox_pr_review` would not make the two paths equivalent at approval time. It would trim seconds off a window that is already minutes long in both paths. (3) The docstring at tasks.py:160-164 names the actual safety guarantee: once the toggle is off, head-changing deliveries retract the stale approval ("safety is never preference-gated"). The remaining consequence is one approval on a bot-authored draft that the user opted into seconds before. (4) The retry countdowns (tasks.py:1150-1155) stretch the delay only while GitHub is rate-limited or failing. That makes an already unlikely coincidence a little wider, not reachable in normal use. This is a speculative race with no practical trigger, and the finding's own validator marked it is_valid=false.
